This is actually in the changelog, https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/changelog_14.html#change-0f9751623e95bf8b19d0467efcd2c479 so I'm not sure if it's just how it works now.

But I agree that it may makes sense to do something a bit smarter here, like `max(dialect_start, minvalue)` if increment is >0 else use maxvalue.

> @gordthompson do you remember the rationale of this change?

While adding sequence support for mssql we discovered that SQL Server defaults its sequences to BIGINT and an initial value of the lowest possible negative BIGINT value (-9.223372037E18). This seemed likely to confuse many people who just assume that sequences will start at 1 so we made that the default and users were free to specify their own start value if they want (or need) to.

would it make sense doing something like this?
- set start at 1 if start not set and no min/max value is set.
- if minvalue is set but start is not do `max(1, minvalue)`. I think we could do this independently of the increment value.
- make `None` a valid value meaning "do not emit the start with in the sql"
Sounds reasonable to me, but I recall that @zzzeek had some pretty firm ideas about how sequences *should* work so I'd wait to see what the boss says. :wink:

i just need Sequence to do the same thing it always has if no parameters are passed.  if passing the relatively new "minvalue" parameter implies a new "start" value, I think ...why dont we just raise an error for this?  they should know to set "start" also in that case.  explicit is better than implicit etc.   are we actually rendering "START AT 1" when "start" is not passed ?

>  are we actually rendering "START AT 1" when "start" is not passed ?

yes, it's in the changelog and all
OK.   well I guess we should just set "start" then
need to document atht too under the "Start" parameter, "if omitted, defaults to minvalue or 1, changed in 1.4.xx etc"

Thanks for looking into this! A few notes:
1. Maybe this behavior should only be for mssql? At least for postgres I know it does "the right thing" when START is omitted:
> The optional clause START WITH start allows the sequence to begin anywhere. The default starting value is minvalue for ascending sequences and maxvalue for descending ones.

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/14/sql-createsequence.html

2. It's also weird to me that `.compile()` modifies the `Sequence`. Maybe it should render the default `START WITH` but not set it on the object?

**Federico Caselli** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**Fix start compiling in a sequence.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4097

Always rendering the start is a bit of a mess, since there are case where we don't know what value we should place to it
I've evidenced some in the tests that probably will render an error.

I think the ambiguous cases here should raise.  we haven't had any further reports of these issues with sequence for the past two years since 1.4 has been released.   so I think the 1.4 community is fine with what we have for now, can we re-milestone back to 2.0/2.x ?
I was treating this as a bugfix for the 1.4 series, but if we change it further I guess we could make this 2.0
